title: Bias of the projected sample
statement: Let $n,a,b,s$ be integers with $n>0$, $a>0$, $2a\le b$, and $s\ge1$. Form the restricted-weight input with dimension $n$, target bias $\varepsilon=a/b$, and Fourier bound $s$. For every set $J$ of coordinates among the $n$ coordinates, choose an index uniformly from the construction's finite, nonempty sample set and project the resulting sample onto $J$. The resulting distribution has every nonzero Fourier coefficient bounded in absolute value by $\varepsilon/(4s)$.
hypotheses_covered: Twice the bias numerator is at most denominator $b$
Fourier bound $s$ is at least one
$J$ is a set of coordinates among the $n$ coordinates
The finite sample set is nonempty
